learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Electrode Impedance.
Apply Electrode Impedance to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Impedance reflects opposition to current at the electrode–skin interface. High or markedly unequal impedance increases noise susceptibility and channel imbalance.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Modern amplifiers tolerate higher absolute impedance than older systems, but low and reasonably balanced impedances remain important. Abrading aggressively can harm skin and is unnecessary.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Checking impedance prevents avoidable artifact and improves confidence in subtle findings.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Chasing an arbitrary ultra-low number can damage skin; ignoring large channel differences can contaminate data.

reviewPrompts.answer: Modern amplifiers tolerate higher absolute impedance than older systems, but low and reasonably balanced impedances remain important. Abrading aggressively can harm skin and is unnecessary.
Checking impedance prevents avoidable artifact and improves confidence in subtle findings.
Chasing an arbitrary ultra-low number can damage skin; ignoring large channel differences can contaminate data.
Aim for safe, stable and balanced contact—not ritualistically perfect numbers.
